block1.content:
# CoTEDS-Smart
CoTEDS-Smart is an extension to the main CoTEDS study. It is focussed on data that is passively collected via smartwatches, fitness trackers and smartphone health apps. At CoTEDS, we are interested in understanding relationships between sleep, physical activity, mental health, and physical health during pregnancy and parenthood. By joining CoTEDS-Smart you would help us learn about these relationships by sharing the high quality data that is passively collected by your fitness tracker.

block2.title: Who can take part in CoTEDS-Smart?
block2.content:
Any TEDS twins and/or coparents enrolled in the Children of TEDS study with their child(ren) are eligible to take part.
We're looking for people who use a smartphone (Apple or Android), Fitbit, Apple Watch, Garmin or Oura Ring.
Participation in CoTEDS-Smart is entirely optional; you can continue taking part in CoTEDS without joining CoTEDS-Smart. You can also join CoTEDS-Smart regardless of whether you have completed your CoTEDS questionnaires.
You can withdraw from the study at any time.

block1.content:
To complement the questionnaire data that you provide, we are interested in exploring relationships using data that is routinely collected by smartwatches, fitness trackers and smartphone apps. Sharing the data collected by them has the potential to provide exciting new scientific insights.

Ultimately this may help to inform the development of better health interventions, and improved treatment during pregnancy, the perinatal period and parenthood.

block2.content: Your data will be collected securely via RADAR-base (managed by Onsentia, developed at King's College London).

blocks.title: What will you use this data for?
blocks.content:
We will collect data from participants' wearable fitness trackers and combine it with other data collected in TEDS and CoTEDS. We will then analyse the combined data to understand associations between fitness tracker data and other indicators of health and wellbeing.

Research questions we can address include:
- Can fitness tracker data collected during pregnancy distinguish between parents who experience perinatal physical/mental health problems and those who do not?
- Does fitness tracker data agree with self-reported questionnaire data on sleep quality and duration?
- Does parenthood lead to an increase or decrease in physical activity?
- How do cardiovascular changes occur over the duration of pregnancy?

Your data will not be shared with anyone other than academic researchers and will not be used for any purpose other than health/wellbeing research.

blocks.title: What does data sharing involve?
blocks.content:
To share the data that your device collects you will need to connect your device on a secure research platform called RADAR-base. From the website you can:
- Check that you can take part
- Sign an electronic consent form
- Set up a study account
- Complete up to 4 tasks to connect your device

We have designed a step-by-step process that will support anyone to connect their device. Completing these steps will take approximately 20 to 35 minutes depending on device (including upload time).

items.title: Who can take part?
items.content: Any CoTEDS participant aged 18 or over who lives in England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man or Guernsey, and who uses a smartphone (Apple or Android), Fitbit, Apple Watch, Garmin or Oura Ring.

items.title: How do I sign up?
items.content: Click the Sign Up Here button and follow the steps to create an account, read the information sheet, give consent, and connect your device.

items.title: What wearable data will you collect?
items.content: With your permission we will collect passive data such as daily activity, sleep duration and quality, and heart-rate metrics from your connected wearable or health app. This helps us link day-to-day patterns with health and wellbeing during pregnancy and parenthood.

items.title: What if I don't own a smartwatch or fitness tracker?
items.content: In the future we hope to be able to provide smartwatches or fitness trackers to some participants who don't already own one (this depends on funding). If you have expressed an interest and we can provide you with a device, we may be in touch by email.

items.title: What is RADAR-base?
items.content: RADAR-base is a secure, open-source research platform based at King's College London, where CoTEDS is also based. It is used to collect data from wearables, smartphones and other devices. In CoTEDS-Smart, RADAR-base connects your device and collects your activity, sleep and related health data so it can be linked with your existing TEDS and CoTEDS information. Data collected via RADAR-base is stored securely at King's College London.

items.title: What is Onsentia?
items.content: Onsentia manages the RADAR-base platform and self-enrolment portal used in CoTEDS-Smart. Onsentia provides the secure technical infrastructure that allows you to connect your device and share your data safely with the CoTEDS research team.

items.title: Are there any incentives for taking part in CoTEDS-Smart?
items.content: As a thank you for taking part, we plan to offer a £10 Love2Shop voucher upon the transfer of the smartwatch data.

blocks.title: Talk to us
blocks.content:
For questions about CoTEDS-Smart, please contact the CoTEDS study team: coteds-project@kcl.ac.uk.
Please note: participation in CoTEDS-Smart is optional and does not affect your continued participation in CoTEDS.

For quick answers to common questions, see our [Frequently Asked Questions](#faq) section above.
